chunks: As for what al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

There is no salat after al-fajr until the sun rises, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Indeed, the sun rises between the two horns of al-shaytan and sets between the two horns of al-shaytan. And he said: There is no salat after al-'asr until you perform al-maghrib.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun; its rising and setting mark the restricted prayer times mentioned
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ: al-shaytan; mentioned in the prophetic wording about sunrise and sunset
key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: the afternoon prayer; after it prayer is restricted until al-maghrib
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn; the morning prayer after which prayer is restricted until sunrise
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the sunset prayer; the endpoint of the restriction after al-'asr
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: salat; the ritual prayer being discussed in terms of its timing
key_terms.قَرْنَيِ: the two horns; part of the prophetic expression describing the sun’s rising and setting

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about performing salat after al-fajr and after al-'asr?
ai.summary: This hadith states that salat is not to be performed after al-fajr until sunrise, and after al-'asr until al-maghrib. It cites a saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the sun’s rising and setting, indicating these as restricted times for prayer.
